findings.source_quote: Ministers of the Gospel today are expected to be soft and effeminate lest they offend their listeners.
findings.suggested_fix: Use standard contemporary Dutch wording. Replace 'effeminé' with 'effeminerend' or better 'effeminé' → 'effeminé' is French and uncommon in Dutch; suggested: 'zacht en effeminé' → 'zacht en effeminé' is odd. Recommended correction: "zacht en vrouwelijk (om anderen niet te kwetsen)" or simply "zacht en effeminerend". Keep original HTML structure and do not alter tags.
findings.translation_quote: Tegenwoordige predikanten van het Evangelie worden verondersteld zacht en effeminé te zijn, opdat zij hun luisteraars niet zouden kwetsen.

findings.source_quote: Bible quotations use a variety of registers (e.g. Psalm 119:165: “Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them”).
findings.suggested_fix:
The translation preserves the quotations but mixes contemporary Dutch with archaic/older Bible-language forms (e.g. 'des Heren', 'den hoge', 'Gij', 'Mij', 'wierd', 'lenspeld'). For consistency and readability in standard contemporary Dutch, consider using a single register for all scripture quotations (modern Dutch Bible phrasing) while preserving chapter and verse numbering exactly. Do not change HTML structure; only adjust the quoted text inside existing

elements.
findings.translation_quote: “Grote vrede hebben zij die uw wet liefhebben: en niets zal hen aanstoot geven” (Psalm 119:165). … “Ik dan, de gevangene des Heren, smeek u, dat gij wandelt waardig naar de roeping waarmee gij geroepen zijt…” (Efeziërs 4:1-2).

findings.suggested_fix: The source's reference title was 'Strongs Concordance'. The translation uses 'Strongs-concordantie' with a hyphen and lowercase 'concordantie'. For fidelity, render the cited work title in conventional Dutch typography but keep it clearly identifiable; suggested: 'Strongs Concordantie' or 'Strong's Concordance' (if the publication's conventional title uses an apostrophe/s). Preserve the <li> text and tags.
